Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleVista Communications Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for joining the question-and-answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleVista Communications' Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Network Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for the third quarter. We exceeded expectations in several key areas. First, we delivered robust net subscriber additions across residential and business segments, totaling 178,000 revenue-generating units, up 12% year-over-year, with residential leading at 153,000 adds driven by fiber deployments and mobile bundling. Second, our content and media segment shone brightly, generating $2.82 billion in revenue, up 18% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $950 million at a 33.7% margin, fueled by 1.8 million paid streaming net adds to reach 48.2 million globally. We are seeing very positive results from our investments in VistaStream, and its subscriber growth and ARPU uplift from premium tiers and ad monetization is significant. Third, we maintained strict discipline on cost of revenue, which came in at $18.7 billion, up just 3.8% year-over-year but improved to 62.7% of revenue, thanks to bandwidth efficiencies and content cost controls. Fourth, our capital investments in networks remain focused and efficient, aligning with our full-year guidance of $18.2 to $19.0 billion, emphasizing 5G enhancements and fiber deep programs. Finally, we are strategically positioning ourselves for margin expansion, guiding to 38% to 40% adjusted EBITDA margins in Q4 and 39% to 41% for full-year 2025, supported by operational savings and revenue mix shifts.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Michael. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $29.8 billion, up 5% year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $10.9 billion, resulting in a margin of 36.5%. We are maintaining strict cost discipline. Capital expenditures were $4.7 billion, primarily allocated to 5G rollout and fiber expansion.

Let me provide more color on our cost of revenue trends, as they highlight our operational leverage. Total cost of revenue stood at $18.7 billion for the quarter, up 3.8% year-over-year from $18.0 billion, but down 1.2% sequentially from Q2's $18.9 billion, which had seasonal boosts from events like the summer Olympics. As a percentage of revenue, it improved 110 basis points year-over-year to 62.7%, demonstrating our focus amid growth in 5G mobile, fiber broadband, and our WaveStream OTT platform.

Breaking it down, network operations costs were $8.4 billion, or 45% of cost of revenue, up 4.1% year-over-year due to 22% higher data traffic from 5G Standalone adoption—our 5G subscribers now at 85 million, up 18% year-over-year—and a 28% surge in WaveStream viewing hours to 45 billion, driven by NBA and UEFA Champions League content. While traffic per user rose 15%, unit bandwidth costs dropped 9.2% to $0.47 per GB through Open RAN at 35% of our radio access network with Nokia and Samsung partners, dynamic spectrum sharing, and AI-optimized base station power management that limited energy costs to a 2% increase at $1.1 billion. Interconnect and peering fees with hyperscalers like AWS and Google Cloud were up $120 million year-over-year from off-net video traffic, and capex amortization added $2.1 billion from our $12 billion fiscal 2024 program, including 40% for mid-band spectrum.

Content acquisition and licensing costs rose 9.5% to $4.9 billion, up $425 million year-over-year, reflecting premium content demands for WaveStream's 32 million subscribers with 1.2% churn. This included escalations in sports rights like ESPN+ equivalents and Bollywood studios, adding $250 million. Regionally, North America was $2.8 billion up 7% from NFL-style packages and Hulu/Disney bundles; EMEA $1.4 billion up 15% amid Premier League and Bundesliga bidding; APAC $0.7 billion up 5% from K-dramas and IPL. We're hedging by shifting 20% of spend to user-generated and AI-curated content via WaveAI, aiming for 5-7% reductions by fiscal 2026.

Customer premises equipment and direct sales support costs fell 2.1% to $3.8 billion, down $85 million, thanks to supply chain normalization. CPE depreciation for handsets, ONTs, and STBs benefited from phasing out 4G subsidies with 5G device penetration at 65%, vendor deals with Apple and Qualcomm at $220 average unit cost, and Corning concessions for fiber ONTs. Other costs like roaming and bad debt were $1.6 billion, up 1.2%, with bad debt at 0.8% of revenue due to AI credit scoring.

Overarching trends show $650 million in run-rate savings from our Efficiency 2.0 program, including virtualized network functions via VMware and Red Hat, 6% lower tower leases, and 12% reduced field ops. Inflation added $200 million, but regional dynamics vary: North America up 3.2%, EMEA up 8.1% from spectrum amortization and roaming caps, APAC flat with vendor financing. For Q4, we expect $19.0 to $19.3 billion, up 4-5% year-over-year, with full-year at $74.5 billion, targeting 60% of revenue by 2027 through 6G R&D, private 5G, and bundling.

Shifting to our content and media segment performance, which is a high-growth engine. Revenue reached $2.82 billion in Q3, up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, driven by a 22% surge in streaming subscriptions to $1.65 billion, 14% ad revenue growth to $750 million from AI dynamic insertion boosting US CPMs 12%, and $430 million from licensing up 9% via Charter renewals and Samsung TV Plus distribution. North America was 72% at $2.03 billion up 20% from VistaStream bundling with fiber broadband at 65% penetration among 18 million postpaid wireless subs; EMEA $520 million up 25% from UEFA Champions League and premium sports in UK/Germany; APAC $280 million up 8% offset by ad softness but aided by 15 million MAUs on VistaStream Free.

Profitability expanded with adjusted EBITDA at $950 million, a 33.7% margin up 320 basis points year-over-year. Cash content spend was flat at $1.2 billion despite 15% more original hours to 2,500, operating income $720 million with $18 billion library amortization over 5-7 years. Churn acquisition costs dropped 10% via ML models covering 90% of subs, and 5G edge caching with Akamai cut delivery 18%.

Subscriber metrics show total paid streaming at 48.2 million, +1.8 million net adds—strongest since Q4 2022—with VistaStream SVOD at 32.5 million +1.2 million QoQ, hybrid bundles 15.7 million +600k. ARPU rose 4.2% to $12.85 from 22% premium tier uptake like VistaStream Ultimate at $17.99 with 4K/HDR, and 5G Home bundles at $15+ blended. SVOD churn at 1.8% down from 2.1%, session times up 14% to 28 hours via AWS AI recs. FAST/AVOD at 42 million MAUs added $180 million ads at 15% CPM growth. This outpaces Netflix adds by 20% and Disney+ margins, thanks to telco distribution.

Strategically, $4 billion annual content shifts 25% to sports like NBA FY2025 and Premier League for 2-3 million international subs, 5G multicast pilots cut live bandwidth 30%, APAC targets 10 million by YE2025 via Jio partnerships, and DSP integrations with Trade Desk/DV360 unlock addressable TV for 100+ million viewers. Q3 guide: $2.9-$3.0 billion revenue 17-20% growth, 34% margins, 1.5-2.0 million adds.

On net subscriber additions by segment, we achieved 178,000 total RGUs, up 12% year-over-year, our 11th straight positive broadband quarter. Residential added 153,000, 86% of total and up 15% year-over-year. Broadband netted 112,000 from passing 450,000 more homes to 28 million footprint, 42% penetration, $118 ARPU up 8% on 2 Gbps plans. Mobile postpaid +28,000 with $52 ARPU, 0.89% churn via AI retention. Video +13,000 from StreamOne bundles with FAST/live sports, despite 1.2% linear churn. Northeast/Sunbelt led with 25% share gains vs. AT&T Fiber.

Business added 25,000, up 5% year-over-year: enterprise 12,000 from SD-WAN/private 5G like hyperscaler edge deals, $1,200 monthly ARPU on 10 Gbps rings; SMB 13,000 via Business Essentials with Wi-Fi 7/VoIP/cybersecurity, 8,000 managed services RGUs, 0.7% churn. Midwest/Southeast strong, Mexico JV +2,000 FWA. Overall churn 0.95%, lowest in two years from $500 million automation/Amdocs investments. Q4 expect 160,000-190,000 adds from 500,000 FTTH passes, promotions, AI private nets. Fiber Everywhere counters Starlink with microwave hybrids for 10-12% growth.

Now, on capital expenditure guidance for network investments, we reaffirm full-year 2024 at $18.2 to $19.0 billion, about 18% of $105 billion revenue midpoint, up 2% from 2023's $17.8 billion amid 4-5% inflation per Deloitte. Wireless is 65% or $11.8-$12.4 billion: $4.5 billion mid-band 5G with massive MIMO on 30,000 sites, 50,000 Open RAN small cells for 25% spectral efficiency on 40% data surge; $2.2 billion mmWave densification in top 50 metros for sub-10ms latency vs. T-Mobile/Dish/Starlink.

Wireline $5.5-$5.8 billion for FiberLink FTTH passing 12 million more locations to hit 10G symmetric, $3.8 billion last-mile/PON, skewed to US Sunbelt/Midwest growth; Europe Vodafone JV $800 million FTTP in Spain/Germany. Media infrastructure $900 million-$1.0 billion for 200 edge nodes with AWS Outposts on 150 million MAUs/22% streaming hours growth, $1.2 billion FWA for 2 million homes at 300Mbps+.

This targets 3-4x five-year ROI from 5G slicing like Siemens pilots, 15% ad yield boosts, despite $500 million inflation/snags offset by 60% Ericsson/Nokia split. $200 million 6G R&D at 7-15 GHz; 2025 intensity 16-17% for $12-13 billion FCF.

Finally, on EBITDA margin guidance, for Q4 2024 we're at 38% to 40%, 150-250 bps expansion from Q3's 36.5%, via $450 million YTD savings from Network AI Optimization like T-Mobile's Intent-Based Networking, cutting opex 8%, postpaid churn 0.9%; 4-5% QoQ wireless growth from Unlimited Max 5G/20% B2B private nets, AetherStream 12% ARPU from ads surpassing 18 million subs; media 45%+ margins on Quantum Realms 25% DTC growth.

North America 85% EBITDA 2-3% expansion on 15% FWA/ $1.2 billion BEAD grants; Europe 32-34% steady with Vodafone \u20ac200 million saves vs. UK price caps; APAC/LatAm high-teens like Indonesia 42% despite forex. Full-year 2025 39-41%, 200-400 bps from 2024's 37%, capex 15-16%, 95% US 5G coverage, edge/Open RAN. 5G slicing/URLLC like $500 million V2X auto OEM; AetherStream bundles 35% broadband attach/50% media margins; premium mmWave/C-band vs. price wars, FCC stability, 2.5% inflation. Risks: chipsets, FWA vs. Comcast DOCSIS, Dish leases; but 45% FCF conversion funds $5 billion buybacks/4.2% yield. Outpacing AT&T 37-39%, Charter 42%.

David Patel: Thank you. I would like to provide an update on our network performance. We have made significant progress in expanding our 5G coverage to 95% in key US markets, with Standalone core deployments leveraging our C-band spectrum from recent FCC auctions. Our network reliability metrics continue to improve, with spectral efficiency up 25% from massive MIMO and AI traffic orchestration, while data usage averages 25 GB per postpaid subscriber, up 15% year-over-year. We've rolled out Open RAN on 35% of sites with Nokia and Ericsson, targeting further per-GB cost declines. We are also actively working on enhancing our cybersecurity infrastructure, including edge computing nodes for low-latency streaming and private networks. Our team's dedication to fiber deep and FWA hybrids has been instrumental in achieving these results, passing 450,000 more homes quarterly and securing grants for rural expansion.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be given at that time. Our first question comes from John Carter with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

John Carter: Good morning. Can you discuss the competitive landscape and your strategy for maintaining leadership in 5G monetization and fiber overbuilds?

Michael Reynolds: Certainly, John. The landscape remains intense with T-Mobile's pricing aggression, Verizon's Fios expansions, Charter's HFC upgrades, and emerging threats like Starlink in rural areas. Our strategy centers on converged offerings: bundling VistaStream with 5G home internet and fiber at 35% attach rates, leveraging our mmWave/C-band spectrum for premium ARPU in metros, and enterprise slicing for V2X and manufacturing private nets, like our OEM pact. FiberLink's 28 million footprint and 42% penetration give us share gains in Sunbelt head-to-heads, while Open RAN and AI efficiencies keep us ahead on costs. We're confident this delivers 10-12% RGU growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for subscriber growth in the next quarter, and how will that impact EBITDA margins?

Lisa Chen: We anticipate Q4 net adds of 160,000 to 190,000 RGUs, supported by 500,000 additional FTTH passes, holiday bundles, and enterprise ramps, with residential broadband and streaming leading. This will drive 4-5% QoQ wireless service growth and media adds of 1.5-2 million, contributing to our 38-40% EBITDA margin guide through favorable mix—60%+ data ARPU, 45%+ media margins—and $450 million AI savings, expanding 150-250 bps sequentially despite traffic growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Kim: Can you provide an update on your fiber deployment plans and the expected ROI on those investments?

David Patel: Absolutely. Our FiberLink program passed 450,000 homes in Q3, targeting 12 million more by year-end for symmetric 10G speeds via GPON/XGS-PON, focused on high-growth US regions like Florida and Texas where housing starts are up 15%. We've secured $1.2 billion BEAD grants for rural fiber, complementing FWA hybrids for 300Mbps+ to 2 million homes. ROI hurdles at 3-4x over five years from $15-20 ARPU uplift, 42% penetration, and bundles boosting broadband attach. Partnerships with Corning and Nokia ensure efficiency, positioning us to outpace AT&T's footprint amid copper retirements.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Michael, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Michael Reynolds: Thank you. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value. Thank you for your time and interest in TeleVista Communications.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
